newsitem.title: UK: British exporters fall victim to strong currency.
newsitem.headline: British exporters fall victim to strong currency.

text.p: The effects of a strong pound continued to lash the British stock market on Thursday, claiming fresh victims among top exporters.

Shares in food and drink group Grand Metropolitan, retail and mail order group Great Universal Stores and media firm Reed all fell amid concerns over sterling, even after the currency slipped from its highs.
However, some major exporters, whose shares have lagged in recent sessions, clawed their way back from their lows.
They recovered as the pound eased from its highs on comments by Bank of England governor Eddie George that quelled fears of an immediate interest rate rise.
George acknowledged the problem for companies, telling a parliamentary committee the pound's rally was beginning to hurt exports.
"I'm sure that it is eating into profit margins or making prices less attractive than they were."

But George also dampened one of the key factors that has helped push sterling to its dizzying heights by saying that although interest rates would have to rise, there was no "urgent need for a dramatic step."

A batch of corporate results on Thursday highlighted how sentiment towards British exporters has changed as the pound has hit four-year peaks against the German mark and dollar, squeezing export margins.
The currency issue is increasingly causing concern as around 50 percent of all sales by British companies are made abroad.

Grand Metropolitan shares fell 10p to 446-1/2p after annual results came in slightly below average forecasts. GrandMet has over 80 percent of its currency transaction exposure hedged forward for 1997, but analysts still focused on the impact of the strong pound against the dollar.
Analysts expect profits for full year 1996/97 to be reduced by some 30 to 40 million pounds (($49 million to $65 million) if sterling stays at current levels and its hedging policy remains unchanged.
BZW strategist Steve Wright said he expected further earnings downgrades to filter through.
"Analysts' forecasts still have to catch up with what sterling has so far done." Wright said.

Great Universal Stores Plc reported lower first half profits today and warned the strong pound may have a significant impact on the results of its overseas subsidiaries. Its shares closed 24-1/2p lower at 651-1/2p in response.
Shares in media group Reed International closed down 61-1/2p at 10.90 pounds, reversing gains which drove the price to 11.89, as analysts downgraded profit forecasts on concern over the pound.

UBS analyst Colin Tennant said the company's trading statement showed that if exchange rates stayed where they were there would be a negative impact on 1997 earnings. "I think people are factoring that in," he said.
ABN AMRO Hoare Govett analyst Richard Jolliffe said he was considering reducing his 1997 pretax profit forecast to 888 million pounds, down 41 million from the previous figure.
He said this was based on the strength of sterling but there were also other fundamental factors depressing the share price. He declined to elaborate.
Jerry Evans, European equity strategist at Enskilda said sterling's effects on British exports will continue and may also impact on performance next year.
"The UK stock market is almost an export driven market and the full impact of the stronger sterling has not yet come through," said Evans. ($1=.6161 Pound)
